To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have characterized the ammonium transport activity of human Rhesus factors variants associated to human diseases or with unknown phenotypes by using a yeast-based functional assay.

(1) the yeast expression assay is an inexpensive, fast, easy and efficient method to characterize human Rhesus factors variants, (2) the HsRhAG I61R and F65S mutations associated to OHSt impair ammonium transport and (3) HsRhCG R202C, a variant associated to metabolic acidosis, also impairs ammonium transport.

the ammonium transport activity of Rh factors is altered by nsSNPs, and that these alterations could be involved in human pathologies.
